newsitem.title: USA: Safeway sees strike hurting results.
newsitem.headline: Safeway sees strike hurting results.

text.p: Safeway Inc said the current strike by unions representing its retail clerks, bakers and meatcutters in Alberta will hurt its sales and operating results for as long as the strike continues.
Safeway said it is unable to determine the extent of the financial impact at this time.

The strike in the Alberta operating area began March 26. Safeway said it continues to operate the 73 affected stores with a combination of replacement workers, management and employees who have returned to work.

Safeway, the second largest food and drug retailer in North America based on sales, posted first quarter earnings of $0.51 a share on sales of $4.07 billion, up from earnings of $0.40 a share on sales of $3.88 billion.
First quarter same-store sales increased 3.6 percent. Gross profit was 28.09 percent of sales in the first quarter of 1997 compared with 28.14 percent in 1996.
Improvements in buying practices and product mix were offset primarily by investments to drive sales in various regions, Safeway said.
During the first quarter, Safeway said it invested $70 million in capital expenditures and opened four new stores.

The total capital expenditures in 1997 for Safeway and the recently acquired Vons Cos Inc are expected to exceed $800 million to open 40 to 45 new stores and complete more than 180 remodels, Safeway said. Safeway completed the acquisition of Vons on April 8.
Increased sales combined with efforts to reduce or control expenses continue to lower operating and administrative expenses as a percentage of sales, Safeway said.
